data.title: Flag Ship Acquisition announces $400M Bluechip business combination
data.description:
• Flag Ship Acquisition (FSHP) has signed a merger agreement to combine with Cayman Islands-based Bluechip & Co. Holdings.
  • The transaction values Bluechip at a Company Net Value of $400M, with Bluechip shareholders set to receive an aggregate of 40M Purchaser ordinary shares.
  • Flag Ship will merge into its newly formed subsidiary, Bluechip Holdings, which will survive as the publicly traded parent company.
  • Bluechip Merger Sub will then merge with Bluechip, making Bluechip a wholly owned subsidiary of the new public parent.
  • Flag Ship shareholders will receive one Purchaser ordinary share for each existing Flag Ship ordinary share, while existing rights will convert into Purchaser rights and ultimately be exchanged for one-tenth of a Purchaser ordinary share each.
  • Bluechip will fund certain Flag Ship transaction expenses through non-interest-bearing loans, which will be cancelled if the acquisition merger closes.
  • The combined company’s board is expected to have five directors, including nominees from Flag Ship and Bluechip and three directors expected to meet Nasdaq independence requirements.
  • Bluechip CEO Ming Zhang and its other officers are expected to become officers of the combined public company.
  • Bluechip’s businesses span insurance-related customer acquisition, financial education, referrals, U.S. capital-markets advisory, AI-driven online advertising and data-center services.

data.title: Novartis' Lutathera now facing generic competition from Cirium's Bexlutry
data.description:
• The US FDA has approved Cirium's radioligand therapy Bexlutry (lutetium Lu 177 dotatate) for receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, the first such generic treatment approved for Novartis' (NVS) Lutathera.
  • Approval was based on bridging data showing a similar biological and chemical profile to Lutathera.
  • Like Lutathera, Bexlutry works by delivering targeted radiation to tumors by binding to somatostatin receptors frequently expressed on the tumors.
  • Novartis reported $436M in Lutathera sales in the first half of 2026.  
  • The approval follows Cirium's August announcement it would acquire Lantheus Holdings (LNTH) in an $8B deal.

data.title: U.S. Dept. of Justice says states should post $1.9B bond in Paramount suit
data.description:
The U.S. Dept. of Justice wants state attorneys general and a trade union suing to block Paramount Skydance's $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) to post a $1.9 billion bond to cover late fees that result from their litigation.

"None of these cases provides a legitimate basis to disregard Section 16’s plain text requiring private persons to post a 'proper bond' before a preliminary injunction may issue," attorneys for the DOJ  wrote in a filing on Monday.

Last Wednesday Paramount (PSKY) continued its campaign to have plaintiffs in a lawsuit seeking to block its merger with Warner Bros. (WBD) post a $1.9 billion surety bond to cover the company’s losses, including ticking fees, if it ultimately prevails.

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount (PSKY) must pay Warner Bros. (WBD) shareholders $650M per quarter beginning October 1. Because the trial is set for March 2027, Paramount would be required to pay $1.3B in ticking fees plus another $190M in incremental financing costs and legal fees.

The plaintiffs, which include twelve state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, argue that Paramount (PSKY) is ineligible for a bond since it was Paramount that agreed to halt the merger.

The judge overseeing the case, Araceli Martínez-Olguín, previously declined to order a bond in July. The federal judge has scheduled a trial start date for  March 2027.

News of the DOJ's push for the states to post a bond was earlier reported by Bloomberg.
